ambiguities.evidence: The same sentence refers to b x b blocks and to the system Ax=b. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
ambiguities.impact: In q=n/b and n-b+1, b is the block size; in (A+Delta A)x_hat=b, it is the right-hand-side vector. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.7)).
ambiguities.issue: The printed theorem overloads the symbol b for both the block size and the right-hand side of Ax=b. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).

ambiguities.evidence: The proof only says that Theorem 4.3 is combined with standard triangular-system error analysis, while section 4 establishes u as the working precision. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: section 4 introduction; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: proof of Theorem 4.4).
ambiguities.impact: The contract may identify standard triangular substitution at working precision u, but cannot add an unstated rounding model for the original right-hand side. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4 and proof).
ambiguities.issue: The word 'substitution' does not explicitly identify the sequence or storage precision of the right-hand side. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).

ambiguities.evidence: The stated algebra is A=LU and L_kk U_kk=A_kk. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: Algorithm 4.1 heading and line 2).
ambiguities.impact: The source contract is the no-permutation A=LU formulation and should not silently generalize (4.7) to a pivoted PA=LU algorithm. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
ambiguities.issue: Algorithm 4.1 contains no permutation matrix, but line 2 does not separately discuss whether an implementation might pivot inside a diagonal block. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: Algorithm 4.1).

ambiguities.evidence: Equation (4.7) adds 2gamma_n+(gamma_n)^2 to the factorization coefficient from (4.4). (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: equation (4.4); PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
ambiguities.impact: The final perturbation must be treated existentially as the combined factorization-plus-substitution perturbation. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4 and proof).
ambiguities.issue: The Delta A in Theorem 4.4 includes solve error and need not be the same perturbation as the Delta A used in Theorem 4.3. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).

contract_plain_english: Provided the right-looking block LU factorization and subsequent triangular substitutions complete, the computed x_hat exactly solves a system with only A perturbed. Equation (4.7) bounds that perturbation componentwise using the computed factors and an exact coefficient containing low-precision conversion, block-FMA accumulation, local block factorization, and both substitution errors, with all mixed and squared terms retained. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.7)).

source_evidence.anchor: standard floating-point model and gamma definitions
source_evidence.observation: The paper defines unaccented, barred, and effective-FMA gamma quantities and assumes their denominators are positive.

Algorithm 4.1 is a right-looking block LU factorization of an n x n matrix given in working precision u. Diagonal factorizations and block triangular solves use u, while trailing updates convert factor blocks to u_low and invoke Algorithm 3.1.
The local LU and triangular-solve results are componentwise backward-error statements. Theorem 4.3 supplies the factorization contribution later combined with substitution in Theorem 4.4.

The theorem states the backward equation (A+Delta A)x_hat=b and the complete componentwise factorization-plus-solve coefficient, including conversion, block-FMA, local factorization, and substitution terms.
The matrix-update analysis inherited by Algorithm 4.1 assumes that underflow and overflow do not occur.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is for the right-looking block LU Algorithm 4.1 followed by substitution, with low-precision conversions confined to the factor blocks used by block-FMA trailing updates. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
binders: Let A be in R^(n x n), partitioned into b_blk x b_blk blocks with q=n/b_blk an integer; b_blk denotes the block size. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).

Let b_rhs be the right-hand side in Ax=b_rhs and let x_hat be the solution produced by substitution; conformability implies b_rhs and x_hat are n-vectors, although the theorem does not state their spaces separately. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
Let L_hat and U_hat be the computed LU factors produced by Algorithm 4.1, and let Delta A be the backward perturbation asserted by Theorem 4.4. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).

Let u be the working/output unit roundoff, u_low the conversion unit roundoff for update operands, bar_u the internal block-FMA unit roundoff, u_FMA the block-FMA output unit roundoff, and tilde_u_FMA the effective rounding parameter. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: section 4 introduction and Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3)).
conclusions: There exists Delta A such that (A+Delta A)x_hat=b_rhs. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).

|Delta A| <= K (|A|+|L_hat||U_hat|) componentwise, where K=2u_low+u_low^2+max(tilde_gamma_{q-1}^FMA+bar_gamma_{n-b_blk+1}+tilde_gamma_{q-1}^FMA bar_gamma_{n-b_blk+1}, gamma_{b_blk})(1+u_low)^2+2gamma_n+(gamma_n)^2. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).

The factorization coefficient through Theorem 4.3 is the part ending after max(...)(1+u_low)^2; combining triangular substitution adds exactly 2gamma_n+(gamma_n)^2. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Theorem 4.3 and equation (4.4); PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: proof of Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.7)).
constants_and_indexing: The number of preceding block updates is indexed by q-1. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).

The internal scalar-arithmetic index is n-b_blk+1, including the +1 from the initial subtraction in an update. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Corollary 4.1 and Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
The competing local block factorization or solve term is gamma_{b_blk}. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
The two full triangular substitutions contribute indices n through 2gamma_n+(gamma_n)^2. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7) and its proof).
definitions_and_conventions: gamma_k=ku/(1-ku), bar_gamma_k=k bar_u/(1-k bar_u), and tilde_gamma_k^FMA=k tilde_u_FMA/(1-k tilde_u_FMA). (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: gamma and accent definitions).

All matrix absolute values are componentwise, and |L_hat||U_hat| is ordinary matrix multiplication of the componentwise absolute-value matrices. (PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: componentwise absolute-value convention; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
A and b_rhs are the unperturbed data in the backward equation; L_hat, U_hat, and x_hat are computed quantities. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
error_notions: Theorem 4.4 is a componentwise backward-error result: the computed x_hat exactly solves a nearby system with the matrix perturbed and the right-hand side unchanged. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
The theorem does not give a forward-error bound for x_hat or a normwise relative backward error. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
exceptional_values: The theorem is conditional on the algorithm producing factors and substitution producing a solution; breakdown cases are outside its conclusion. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
The triangular-solve result used in the proof assumes a nonsingular triangular coefficient matrix. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Lemma 4.2).
Underflow and overflow are excluded in the inherited matrix-update analysis, and NaNs or infinities are not modeled. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).
higher_order_terms: Equation (4.7) retains u_low^2, the mixed gamma product, (1+u_low)^2, and (gamma_n)^2. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).

The coefficient in (4.7) is not a dominant-term or big-O approximation; the dominant-term specializations appear only later in Table 4.1. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7) and paragraph introducing Table 4.1).

The inherited Algorithm 3.1 analysis simplifies possible double rounding by retaining one rounding and supplies no explicit remainder for the omitted one. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: double-rounding paragraph before (3.2)).
hypotheses: A is supplied in working precision u and Algorithm 4.1 uses precision u for diagonal block factorization and block triangular solves. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: section 4 introduction and Algorithm 4.1 lines 2 and 4).
Algorithm 4.1 produces L_hat and U_hat, and subsequent substitution produces x_hat for Ax=b_rhs. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
Trailing updates convert computed factor blocks to u_low and evaluate the update with Algorithm 3.1 and a b_blk x b_blk block FMA. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: Algorithm 4.1 lines 8-9).
The standard floating-point model holds and k times each relevant unit roundoff is less than one. (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: equations (2.3)-(2.4) and gamma definition).
The update analysis assumes no underflow or overflow. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).
implicit_context: The proof combines the factorization backward error from Theorem 4.3 with the standard error analysis for solving triangular systems. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: proof of Theorem 4.4).

Successful production of the factors and solution implicitly requires the necessary block factorizations and triangular solves to complete; Lemma 4.2 states its solve result for a nonsingular triangular matrix. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
Algorithm 4.1 states the factorization as A=LU and introduces no permutation matrix. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: Algorithm 4.1 heading and body).
norms: No norm appears; |Delta A|, |A|, |L_hat|, and |U_hat| are componentwise absolute-value matrices. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
numerical_model: Unaccented gamma terms use working precision u, barred gamma terms use the internal block-FMA precision bar_u, and tilde_gamma^FMA uses the prioritized effective rounding parameter from (3.3). (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: gamma accent convention; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3)).

Converting L_hat and U_hat blocks to u_low contributes componentwise perturbations bounded by u_low and produces the exact term 2u_low+u_low^2. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: proof of Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).

Block update arithmetic contributes tilde_gamma_{q-1}^FMA, bar_gamma_{n-b_blk+1}, and their product, while local block factorization or triangular solves contribute gamma_{b_blk}. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Theorem 4.3 and proof; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).

undebatable_constraints: The matrix is n x n, the block size divides n, and q=n/b_blk. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
The backward equation perturbs A but leaves the right-hand side unchanged. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
The bound is componentwise and is scaled by |A|+|L_hat||U_hat|. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
The max term is max(tilde_gamma_{q-1}^FMA+bar_gamma_{n-b_blk+1}+tilde_gamma_{q-1}^FMA bar_gamma_{n-b_blk+1}, gamma_{b_blk}). (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
The exact solve contribution is 2gamma_n+(gamma_n)^2 and must not be omitted. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
All second-order terms shown in (4.7) are part of the stated coefficient. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
